sections.content: You know *hay que* + infinitive from A1 Unit 18: *Hay que trabajar*. It never changes for the person, because it names no one: the need belongs to everybody. At B2 that is exactly its job. It is the pattern of notices, instructions and general advice: *Para entrar, hay que mostrar el pasaporte*. It has one form for each tense, always in the third person: *hay que*, *había que*, *habrá que*, *habría que*. The conditional makes it softer, like a suggestion: *Habría que hablar con ella* is "We should talk to her".
sections.title: Everybody, and nobody in particular
hay que
rows: Para entrar, hay que mostrar el pasaporte.
To get in, you have to show your passport.
Antes había que esperar horas para entrar.
In the past you had to wait hours to get in.
Tomorrow we will have to arrive early.
Habría que hablar con ella antes de decidir.
We should talk to her before deciding.

sections.content: Compare *Hay que salir temprano* (what the situation asks of everyone) with *Tengo que salir temprano* (my own need). Never put a person into *hay que*: not *hay que yo salir*. If you want to name who has to act, use *tener que*.
